lines.text: Riya asks her college placement bot: how many active backlogs are allowed? The answer is one sentence, on page four of a forty-page policy.
But the model never reads the whole PDF. It only sees the few chunks you retrieve. So how you cut the document decides everything.
Cut the chunks too large, and each one mixes many topics. Retrieval gets noisy, and you pay to send filler.
Cut them too small, and they lose context. It must be cleared before the drive. What is it?
So start at around five hundred tokens per chunk. But a fixed cut can slice Riya's sentence in half, and neither chunk holds the answer.
The fix is overlap. Repeat about fifty tokens from the end of one chunk at the start of the next.
Now the sentence survives whole in at least one chunk. Better still, split on paragraphs and sentences, not character counts.
Give every chunk an ID card: the file name and the page number. That becomes your citation later.
Then measure. Chunk the same PDF three ways, ask the same questions, and keep the one that retrieves the right passage.
Remember this: bad chunking ruins good models. Start at five hundred tokens with fifty of overlap, then measure.
Next lesson: the full RAG pipeline, with citations.
